_comment: DENISE, AT THE REDFERN SERVICE CENTRE.
A node has a line and up to six choices. A choice may go to another node, or
accept a quest, or turn one in, and may be gated on level, faction, a story
flag, the absence of one, or money. `cost` spends through the wallet and the
server takes it, not the client.
TWO NODES HERE ARE MARKED `improv`. When SYDNEY_DIALOG_AI_URL/_KEY are set,
the server renders those lines through the model once per node per week and
caches the answer. With no key -- which is the ordinary configuration -- the
authored `line` below serves and nothing anywhere is different. An improv
node may not accept, turn in or charge for anything: the schema forbids it
and verifyDialog refuses a pack that tries. The AI paints; the data decides.
THE LADMASTER AND RABBITOHS RAY ARE THE FIRST THING IN THE GAME.
He stands in Sydney Park 45 m from the spawn pin, on the bearing to Redfern,
and he is the only giver in content/ with "marker": "hero" -- a giant `!`
seen from 400 m instead of 150 (world/questmarkers.ts) and a street light of
his own (world/giverlamp.ts), because Sydney Park has no lamps in it: the
nearest is 256 m away, measured off the bake. His quest carries
"bike": true, so accepting it puts a lime bike within five metres.
Ray is on the footpath out the front of the Centrelink, 28 m from Denise --
far enough to clear content-check's 25 m rule between givers, near enough
to read as "out the front". He gives nothing; he only takes the tutorial
back, which is why the quest's giver is the Ladmaster and its turn-in is
on Ray's tree. His numbers about the claim are game/cash.ts's real ones
($100, seven in-game days, per office, six metres from the door) and his
complaint is DeFAULT's Click & Collect, teams.ts id 31.

nodes.line: Oi. Oi bruv. Yeah you, the one standin in the park doin nothin. Come here a sec, I've got somethin for ya.

Adlay, you need some more ascay! Get down to Cenno and tell em you did 5 job interviews this week, eshay bruv! Grab this lime bike and ride down to the fern cuz, its just straight down here then right!
Adlay. Lad. Ascay, cash. Cenno's just Cenno, everyone knows that one. Ya either keep up or ya don't, and if ya don't thats fine, plenty do not.
Five. Dont say six, six is greedy and they check six. Five is the number where the lady goes mm and ticks the box and nobody has to have a day about it.
Nobody's ever asked me that bruv. I'm the Ladmaster. I stand under this light and I tell blokes where the money is. Been doin it since before they done up the kilns.
The fern cuz. Straight down here, then right. Big square, glass front, blokes on the bench out the front. If ya lost the bike thats on you, I only had the one.
Suit yaself ay. Bike stays here then. Its not even my bike.
See? Told ya bruv. Rays alright, but dont let him start on the footy, youll be there til Tuesday.
Gday champ. Nah I'm not in the queue, I was done by half nine. I just like the bench. Sun hits it about now and nobody bothers ya.

choices.text: Bloke in the park sent me.

nodes.line: Him. Course it was him. Here, tenner, dont spend it in there. And now ya know where the door is, which is the actual thing he sent ya for, whatever he told ya.

Right there champ. Glass front, other side of the square, Denise is on the counter and she has heard it. Six metres from that door is close enough. Any closer and it doesnt love ya more, I have tested it.
Hundred bucks. Once every seven days, and a day here is that sun goin round once, not a Monday to a Monday. Per office, mind. Thats the bit nobody reads.

Thirty one doors in this town and the clock is per door. Marrickville, Campsie, Bankstown, Hurstville. Get a car and thats four hundred before lunch. Thats not rortin it champ, thats it workin as designed.
No. No we do not. Some of these DeFAULT fellas have got a knack on em -- Click and Collect, they call it, like its a Woolies order. Five days instead of seven. FIVE.
Thats not the whole of it. Anyone from DeFAULT claims within two hundred metres of one of em and the fella just standin there gets twenty bucks. For standin there. Champ. I stand here all day.
Mate. They took my club out of the competition in 2000 and I came back in 2002 and I have not missed a home game since. I am not changin sides for twenty dollars and a shorter week.
Go the Bunnies. See, thats the right answer and ya didnt even have to think about it. Sit down, theres room.

improv.persona: Rabbitohs Ray, on the bench outside the Redfern service centre. South Sydney supporter since 1988, sixties, warm, aggrieved about everything except the football, which he is aggrieved about differently. Broad Australian, no swearing, no exclamation marks.
improv.context: A stranger has just said go the Bunnies to him unprompted, outside Centrelink in Redfern, which is the correct thing to have said. He is pleased and is not going to make a fuss about being pleased.

nodes.line: Get off my bench.
Take a number. The number is not connected to anything, but take one.

choices.text: What am I meant to be doing?

nodes.line: Your mutual obligations. You agreed to these. There is a signature and it is yours.
Let's see it, then. I'll put it in the system. The system is down. I'll put it in when it's up.
Resilience in the Modern Workplace. Six hours. There's a certificate. Nobody has ever asked to see one.
It leads to the next course.
Forty minutes. It says twelve on the screen. The screen is aspirational.

improv.persona: Denise, a Centrelink officer at the Redfern service centre in Sydney. Twenty-two years in the job, entirely out of patience, not unkind. Deadpan, lower case, very Australian.
improv.context: A claimant has asked how long the wait is. The queue display says twelve minutes and is wrong. She has said this sentence several thousand times.

choices.text: It said twelve when I got here.

nodes.line: It said twelve when I got here in 2004.
This is a participation review. It is not a breach. A breach has a form. This has a conversation, and then possibly a form. — Someone in a high-vis vest is standing in the doorway looking at you.

Don't. They come in here recruiting. Marita reckon they can get you work by Thursday and DeFAULT reckon work is the problem. Whichever one you talk to first is the one you end up with. — Denise goes back to her screen.

improv.persona: Denise, a Centrelink officer at the Redfern service centre in Sydney, twenty-two years in the job and finished with all of it. Deadpan, lower case, no exclamation marks.
improv.context: A recruiter from one of the two street factions -- Marita, who promise work, and DeFAULT, who say work is the problem -- is loitering in the doorway of her office waiting for the claimant to come out. She has watched this happen to a great many people and has no opinion she is paid to share. Spell the two names exactly as Marita and DeFAULT.

nodes.line: I'm a public servant. I'd pick the one that doesn't come to my counter.
